title: Microsoft Purview: Microsoft Graph APIs for archive mailboxes as EWS retires (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing's migration deadline, roadmap status, controls and archiving entitlement are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite the government-cloud roadmap item and explicitly identify the beta examples as preview, not supported for production.

claims.claim: Microsoft is adding Microsoft Graph access to archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: Graph archive support covers the main archive.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The auxiliary archives are created through auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: An archive mailbox can include a main archive mailbox and one or more auxiliary archive mailboxes (created through autoexpanding archive).

claims.claim: The roadmap goal is a single seamless archive view across auxiliary mailboxes.
claims.quote: The goal is to give users a single, seamless Archive view, even though Archive data may physically reside across multiple auxiliary mailboxes

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph now supports importing archive mailbox data.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph now supports exporting archive mailbox data.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph supports managing archive mailbox folders, including auto-expanding archives.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: Organisations using auto-expanding archives must update applications for Graph archive mailbox behaviour.
claims.quote: Organizations using auto-expanding archive mailboxes must update applications to support Microsoft Graph archive mailbox behaviors.

claims.claim: A folder can appear in the main archive while its contents reside in an auxiliary archive.
claims.quote: In some cases, a folder appears in the main archive mailbox, but its contents actually reside in an auxiliary archive mailbox.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Accessing an archive folder whose content is auxiliary can return HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect.
claims.quote: When you access a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary archive mailbox, the API returns an HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect with a Location header.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Exported items in auto-expanded folders can return ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently instead of data.
claims.quote: When you export items from a mailbox that has autoexpanded archive folders, some items in the response might include an ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently error instead of data.

claims.claim: The application repeats the redirected export against the URL provided in the error.
claims.quote: Reissue the export request for those items using the URL provided in the error message.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An import into an auxiliary archive folder can return HTTP 409 Conflict naming the correct mailbox.
claims.quote: When you attempt to import an item into a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary (autoexpanded) archive mailbox, you receive an HTTP 409 Conflict response that indicates the correct target mailbox.

claims.claim: Resolving that import failure requires a new import session targeting the indicated mailbox.
claims.quote: create a new import session targeting the mailbox ID indicated in the error message

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Archive requests must use folder IDs rather than well-known folder names.
claims.quote: Well-known folder names aren't supported for archive mailboxes. Reference folders in archive mailboxes by folder ID rather than by well-known folder name.

claims.claim: The mailbox export APIs export items in full fidelity.
claims.quote: These items can be exported as an opaque stream in full fidelity (you can't change the export stream).

claims.claim: Items can be imported into the same mailbox or a different mailbox.
claims.quote: Items can be imported to the same mailbox or a different one.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the mailbox import and export APIs are not designed for backup and restore.
claims.quote: The mailbox import and export APIs in Microsoft Graph aren't designed for mailbox backup and restore.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The v1.0 import and export overview describes primary and shared mailbox support.
claims.quote: These APIs support access to data in users' primary mailboxes and shared mailboxes on Exchange Online.

claims.claim: The concept overview also explicitly includes archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: These APIs support access to data in users' primary, shared, and archive mailboxes on Exchange Online.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The EWS deprecation parity table targets Import-Export (Archive) for Q4 CY2026.
claims.quote: | Import-Export (Archive) | Export and import mailbox items in archive mailboxes in a full-fidelity format. | Q4 CY2026 |

claims.claim: The EWS deprecation parity table targets In-Place Archive (Generic CRUD) for Q4 CY2026.
claims.quote: | In-Place Archive (Generic CRUD) | Access and manage mailbox items in an existing In-Place Archive. This capability doesn't create archive mailboxes. | Q4 CY2026 |

claims.claim: The In-Place Archive capability does not create archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: This capability doesn't create archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: Learn calls the parity dates estimates that might change.
claims.quote: Estimated availability dates are targets and might change.

claims.claim: The EWS report is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Reports > Usage > Reports > Exchange > EWS usage.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Exchange. ... On the report page, select the EWS usage tab.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the EWS usage report is documented, and the Graph usage reports list has no EWS report.
claims.quote: Searched: 'EWS usage report Microsoft Graph beta API PowerShell Exchange usage report download'; opened ews-usage, graph/api/resources/report and beta reportRoot; searched beta reportRoot for EWS/Web Services. No EWS report operation found.

claims.claim: The tenant report displays SOAP actions per application ID rather than configuring application access.
claims.quote: The Exchange Web Services (EWS) usage report displays the SOAP actions used by each application calling EWS in your organization.

claims.claim: EWS report usage data is collected and aggregated weekly.
claims.quote: Usage data is collected and aggregated weekly, not daily.

claims.claim: EWS usage can take up to 10 days to appear in the report.
claims.quote: It can take up to 10 days for usage to show in the report.

claims.claim: EWS blocking is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Show all > Settings > Org Settings > Security and Privacy > Baseline Security Mode > Authentication > Disable organization-wide access to Exchange Web Services (EWS).
